Generate an actual image, not a written description. Wide 16:9 concept art for the central playable office of an original political strategy game. Camera from the player's chair, slightly elevated, looking across a modest local elected official's wooden desk toward a rain-streaked window and the city at dusk. The desk and its objects are the clear focal point; leave a calm dark margin at the top for an eventual UI title. Seven clearly separated, believable navigation objects: a green rotary telephone on the left, a thick ivory folder at the center with a small lime paper tab, a folded newspaper at the right with empty masthead and abstract non-letter print strokes, a world-map table surface partially visible behind the desk, a window framing the city, a worn closed account ledger on a side shelf, and a wall calendar made of blank squares near the window. A desk lamp makes a warm pool of light. No person, no icons, no interface labels, no floating panels. Strong readable silhouettes, tactile ink and gouache brushwork, sober civic furniture with a few traces of personal ambition. The room should feel like the beginning of a career, intimate and playable, never a generic luxurious presidential room. Make this a beautiful game scene with distinct clickable objects, not a photograph or an admin interface.

Generate an actual high-resolution image sheet, not a written description. Use the attached office as the approved artistic reference for palette, light, paper, atmosphere and painterly handling. This is a cohesive concept board for a political strategy video game. EXACT grid: TWO columns and THREE rows, SIX equal rectangular panels, each panel landscape 16:9, entire sheet ratio 32:27. Straight clean dividing lines, no thick gutters, no overlapping panels, no labels and absolutely no letters or numbers anywhere. All six panels must be fully painted concepts, not plain wireframes. Increase visible gouache brushwork, not photographic detail. Make each panel have one unmistakable focal point and calm spaces where eventual HTML text can sit.

TOP LEFT — DECISION CARD: a tactile ivory dossier on a deep forest-green tabletop. Its upper half is an editorial illustration of a bus depot at dusk: three fictional transit workers in coats face an elected official, buses and a small crowd behind, blank placards. This is a strike negotiation, no violence. Bottom half is quiet ivory paper with two broad understated dark-green option strips and room above them for an eventual headline. A small square fictional advisor bust portrait is inset at the lower-left margin, thoughtful older woman with cropped silver hair. A tiny lime tab marks the decision. No text, no pseudo-writing, no dashboard widgets.

TOP RIGHT — PARLIAMENT VOTE NIGHT: iconic overhead three-quarter view of a civic parliamentary chamber, seats in a clear broad semicircle around a lit wooden speaking podium. Five restrained fictional group colors: moss, muted teal, ochre, dusty plum, slate blue. A few acid-lime seats catch the eye. Clearly separated seat dots within rows; dramatic deep-green shadow surrounds the chamber. A small empty ivory lower strip is reserved for the eventual live vote count. This painting is an atmosphere reference; the actual seats will be SVG in code. No flags or national symbols, no text.

MIDDLE LEFT — PRESS FRONT PAGE: one large ivory newspaper front page lying straight on a dark desk with restrained ink borders, ample empty masthead band and generous empty headline band. A strong ink/gouache vignette of a fictional middle-aged female politician at a microphone with reporters below the headline band. Abstract rectangular areas mark two short article columns but NO glyphs, lines of fake words or readable print. One tiny satirical sketch of an empty swivel chair. A narrow quiet dark-green strip at the right reserved for social reactions. It must immediately feel like an opinionated political newspaper, not a list of uniform cards.

MIDDLE RIGHT — WORLD CAMPAIGN MAP: recognizable world continents viewed as a dramatic dark relief map on aged parchment: Americas on the left, Europe/Africa near center, Asia/Oceania on the right. Stylized terrain, calm deep-green seas, restrained moss/ochre/teal territorial washes, small generic rectangular pennant army standards, thin warm trade arcs across the Atlantic and Pacific, two restrained carmine sanction marks. One highlighted country at the center draws the eye; empty lower-right ivory inset reserved for a leader card. No real flags, no labels, no invented text. This is an art direction reference, not final cartography; exact geography will be drawn in code from open data.

BOTTOM LEFT — CHARACTER BIOGRAPHY CARD: a distinctive entirely fictional 36-year-old Latin American woman politician with dark curly hair pulled back, angular expressive face, dark-green jacket and plain ivory blouse, quietly determined without glamour. Painted bust portrait on the left half of an ivory civic identity dossier; plain green paper backing, warm window light. Right half has one large calm empty biography area and five simple thin horizontal attribute bars below, no numbers or writing. One small lime paper tab. A personal human portrait must dominate, not charts; no seal, logo, photo realism or likeness of any real politician.

BOTTOM RIGHT — NATIONAL OFFICE VARIANT: a wider and more authoritative elected leader's office, same visual language as the attached modest office, warm desk lamp at night, rain on tall windows, visible city. Foreground folder with lime tab, green phone, newspaper, world map table and ledger; all distinct and separated. No luxurious palace, no real emblem or flags. The space and skyline express earned career progression. No person, no text or UI panels.
